transcript: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Over the past year our team has built a tool that helps people improve the way they speak. It listens to a recording, compares it with a clear example of the same message, and shows exactly where the delivery changed. For instance, you might speak too quickly during a key point, or pause for too long before an answer. The tool marks those moments on a timeline, explains what it measured, and suggests one simple change. We tested it with students, teachers, and engineers, and most of them improved within a single week. Today I will show you how it works, step by step. Please feel free to ask questions at any time.

flaws.explanation: 24.1–26.0 s: a pause of 1.90 s inside a phrase after “quickly” and before “during”, 1.66 s longer than the baseline mean pause of 0.24 s (30.09 standard deviations above it). Flagged because the pause was more than 2.0 standard deviations longer than the baseline mean, which is a longer break than in the baseline delivery.
flaws.recommendation: Keep these words connected: aim for a pause close to 0.24 s, as in the baseline delivery.
warnings: The pause type (within a phrase or between sentences) is inferred from the transcript's punctuation.

flaws.explanation: 39.3–50.6 s: speech rate averaged 85.9 words/min, 37.5% below the 137.5 words/min the baseline readings had for these same words (16.64 standard deviations below it), covering “We” to “single”. Flagged because the pace of this run of words was more than 4.0 standard deviations below the baseline's pace for the same words over at least 0.5 s, which indicates slower delivery compared with the baseline.
flaws.recommendation: Bring the pace up in this stretch towards about 137.5 words/min, the pace the baseline readings had for these words, and link phrases together without long gaps.
warnings: Speech rate is compared word by word with the baseline's reading of the same words, after allowing for the speaker's overall pace. The finding is the run of words that differs most, so its start and end are word boundaries, as accurate as the forced alignment is.

overall_summary: 2 delivery deviations from the baseline were detected in 59.7 s of analysed speech (too slow: 1, excessive pause: 1). Deviation score: 90.3 out of 100 across speech rate, pitch, pauses and energy (100 means no deviation was detected). These results compare delivery with the baseline recording; they are not a measure of speech quality or content. Detection thresholds and score weights are initial values that have not yet been calibrated on recorded data.

notes.message: Detection thresholds and score weights are initial values that have not been calibrated on recorded data; treat findings and scores as indicative.
